criteria.label: 1. Understands the main idea of spoken/audio-visual material (10 pts.)
2. Identifies and recalls supporting details (10 pts.)
3. Makes logical inferences from the content (10 pts.)
4. Accurately decodes meaning from tone, intonation, or visuals (10 pts.)
5. Summarizes or paraphrases spoken/audio-visual material meaningfully (10 pts.)
6. Responds appropriately to closed, semi-open, and open-ended questions (10 pts.)
7. Participates in follow-up discussions or group tasks (10 pts.)
8. Demonstrates critical thinking or reflective comments about the material (10 pts.)
9. Uses note-taking or visual strategies (e.g. charts, lists) effectively if needed (10 pts.)
10. Takes turns, listens actively, and engages respectfully in collaborative settings (10 pts.)

criteria.label: Clarity

levels.label: Needs Improvement (1)
levels.descriptor: The speech is very unclear, making it significantly difficult for the listener to understand.

levels.label: Limited (2)
levels.descriptor: The speech is often unclear, and the listener struggles to understand.

levels.label: Good (3)
levels.descriptor: Most speech is clear, with minor issues with a few words, but understanding is not affected.

levels.label: Excellent (4)
levels.descriptor: The speech is clear and easy to understand, with no ambiguity.

criteria.label: Fluency

levels.label: Needs Improvement (1)
levels.descriptor: The speech is very hesitant, with significant pauses, making it choppy and difficult to follow.

levels.label: Limited (2)
levels.descriptor: Frequent pauses or hesitations disrupt the flow of the speech.

levels.label: Good (3)
levels.descriptor: The speaker is generally fluent, with occasional pauses but maintains the flow.

levels.label: Excellent (4)
levels.descriptor: The speaker talks smoothly and naturally with minimal hesitation.

criteria.label: Accuracy

levels.label: Needs Improvement (1)
levels.descriptor: Pronunciation errors are numerous, with fundamental issues affecting understanding.

levels.label: Limited (2)
levels.descriptor: Pronunciation errors are frequent, with several sounds or words mispronounced.

levels.label: Good (3)
levels.descriptor: Most sounds and words are pronounced correctly, with a few minor errors not affecting overall understanding.

levels.label: Excellent (4)
levels.descriptor: Pronunciation of sounds and words is consistently correct, with no noticeable errors.

criteria.label: Intonation

levels.label: Needs Improvement (1)
levels.descriptor: Intonation is inappropriate, making the speech monotonous and ineffective at conveying meaning.

levels.label: Limited (2)
levels.descriptor: Intonation is inconsistent and does not enhance meaning, occasionally leading to misunderstandings.

levels.label: Good (3)
levels.descriptor: The speaker generally has good intonation with some variations but may lack emphasis in certain areas.

levels.label: Excellent (4)
levels.descriptor: The speaker uses appropriate intonation patterns that enhance meaning.

criteria.label: Effective Turn-taking — Waits for the peer to finish speaking before taking a turn.
Effective Turn-taking — Paces responses naturally, neither too quickly nor too slowly.
Effective Turn-taking — Maintains balanced speaking time with peer, allowing an even flow of conversation.
Attentive Listening — Listens actively and attentively to the peer without distractions.
Attentive Listening — Shows engagement by nodding, summarising, or reflecting on the peer’s points.
Attentive Listening — Avoids interrupting the peer and waits for them to complete their thought.
Engaging in Effective and Meaningful Communication — Asks open-ended questions to involve the peer in conversation.
Engaging in Effective and Meaningful Communication — Provides verbal encouragement (e.g. “That’s interesting! Tell me more.”) to promote open dialogue.
Engaging in Effective and Meaningful Communication — Encourages the peer to share more by showing genuine interest in their thoughts and opinions.
Response Quality — Demonstrates thoughtful responses that show understanding of the peer’s message.
Response Quality — Reflects on the peer’s statements before adding her/his own ideas, demonstrating consideration for their input.
Response Quality — Uses relevant questions or comments to deepen conversation based on the peer’s statements.
Response Quality — Avoids short or minimal responses; adds ideas or reflections to maintain flow.
Concluding the Conversation — Wraps up conversation collaboratively, allowing the peer a final turn to add or clarify any points.
Concluding the Conversation — Ensures both sides feel heard and understood before concluding the discussion.
Concluding the Conversation — Ends on a positive note, expressing gratitude or summarising main ideas with mutual agreement.

levels.descriptor: Does not use target grammatical structures or makes errors that severely hinder communication.

levels.label: Limited (2)
levels.descriptor: Makes frequent grammatical errors that often make it difficult to understand her/him.

levels.label: Satisfactory (3)

levels.label: Satisfactory (3)

levels.label: Good (4)

levels.label: Excellent (5)
levels.descriptor: Actively listens to and builds on others’ ideas, supports group members, and contributes meaningfully to discussions.

levels.label: Satisfactory (3)
levels.descriptor: Follows task instructions, but with occasional lapses or incomplete adherence.

levels.label: Good (4)
levels.descriptor: Follows task instructions well with only minor deviations or omissions.

levels.label: Excellent (5)
levels.descriptor: Fully adheres to task instructions, ensuring all guidelines are followed precisely and producing high-quality work.
